open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity and repeated admission
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict.” conflicts with “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions,” because those TrialExecutions are newly minted entities and are themselves a field of the verdict.
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again against the same unchanged corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, replaced, or is a distinct verdict created for the newly minted TrialExecutions?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and its original TrialExecutions
Create a distinct verdict for each admission run
Replace the prior verdict's referenced TrialExecutions
open_points.default_guess: Create a distinct immutable verdict for each admission run.

open_points.subject: ProofResult identity across mutable binding state
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result.” conflicts with the carried decision that “a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).”
open_points.question: Is a ProofResult identified by the flow version alone, or by the flow version together with the binding and manifest facts observed when proof is computed, so that one version can have different results over time?
options: One stable result per flow version
A new value for each distinct proof result under the currently observed dependencies
No persistent identity; each proof is only an ephemeral computation
open_points.default_guess: Treat each computed result as an ephemeral value whose facts may differ when dependencies change.

open_points.subject: Run terminal status after guarded skips
open_points.text: “The run is ... `succeeded` when every node and output concluded successfully” does not say whether a `skipped_by_guard` node or flow output counts as having concluded successfully.
open_points.question: When all executed work succeeds but one or more nodes or outputs are `skipped_by_guard`, does the run end `succeeded`, end under another existing status, or remain non-final?
